column3: “The opposer” is rendered “the enemy,” and “told” as “disclosed.”
“Repeated” is rendered “again,” and “sought favor to him” as “implored him.” “Take away the evil” is rendered “avert the evil scheme.”
“The letters, the plan of Haman” is rendered “the letters devised by Haman.”
“How will I be able and I will look on” is rendered “how can I endure to see.”
“Here!” is rendered “Behold,” and “his hand” as “his hands.”
“According to the good in your eyes” is rendered “as you see fit.”
“Cush” is rendered “Ethiopia,” and “writing” as “script.” NASB uses parentheses.
“The riders of the royal steeds, the sons of the mares” is rendered “riding on steeds sired by the royal stud”; the meaning of the words for the horses is uncertain.
“Make a stand on their life” is rendered “defend their lives.” The Hebrew may mean the enemies' children and women; NASB has “including children and women.”
“Riders of the royal steeds” is rendered “riding on the royal steeds”; the meaning of the Hebrew words is uncertain.
“A day good” is rendered “a holiday,” and “becoming Jews” as “became Jews.”
